name: Transitions and composition
observations: OpenMontage is inspected at revision 195eab24478dc9363326aec437aefc3701635ddf; its repository LICENSE is AGPL-3.0 (LICENSE:1-3,10-25). The relevant renderer is the standalone remotion-composer package, whose package manifest declares Remotion 4.0.484 and @remotion/transitions 4.0.484 (remotion-composer/package.json:1-23), but no source import of @remotion/transitions was found; transition behavior is implemented with Remotion Sequence, interpolate, spring, CSS transforms, opacity, and clip paths.

The Explainer input model represents cuts with in_seconds/out_seconds, optional type/source, animation, transition_in, transition_out, and transition_duration, plus overlay timing and audio configuration (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:187-268,270-308).

The main Explainer maps every cut to a Remotion Sequence whose start and duration are rounded from seconds using the composition fps; overlays use the same independent time-window model (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:834-870). Captions are a separate layer and narration/music are separate audio layers (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:872-917).

VideoScene derives the local scene duration from sceneDurationSeconds, treats transition tokens cut and none as hard edges, otherwise linearly fades in and out over transitionFrames, and seeks source media with startFrom (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:417-474). The default transition duration is effectively 8 frames because transition_duration defaults to 8/fps seconds; supplied transition_duration is converted to rounded frames and clamped to at least one frame (same file:438-456).

ImageScene supplies image-scene motion choices zoom-in, zoom-out, pan-left, pan-right, ken-burns/ken-burns-slow-zoom, parallax, or static/none, using clamped normalized frame progress plus spring entrance and a final opacity reduction (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:342-411).

AnimeScene accepts one to four images, computes an effective local duration because useVideoConfig durationInFrames is the full composition duration, divides that local duration into image segments, and overlaps adjacent opacity windows by about 1.2 seconds to avoid zero-opacity gaps (remotion-composer/src/components/AnimeScene.tsx:27-55,146-227). It also applies camera motion, optional lighting gradient, vignette, and deterministic particle overlay (same file:75-126,230-284).

CollageBurst defines six explicit card-entry transition names: pop, slide-zoom, spin, shutter, glitch, and swoop (remotion-composer/src/CollageBurst.tsx:19-25). Each card computes in/out frames from seconds, uses spring-based entry and exit, applies transition-specific transforms/opacity/blur/clip-path, and renders video content inside a Sequence starting at the card in-frame (same file:213-362). It also uses seeded deterministic jitter and composition-level screen shake around entries (same file:224-242,288-307,450-460).

ProgressBar clamps public progress to 0-100 and supports fill, pulse, and step modes; fill timing is interpolated against the composition duration, pulse adds a bounded sinusoidal modulation after fill, and step discretizes progress into segment-count or five steps (remotion-composer/src/components/ProgressBar.tsx:9-15,50-109). It provides segmented bars with per-segment springs and labels, optional percentage display, and fixed 1920-based track geometry (same file:111-128,186-279).

Root provides theme-level transitionDuration values of 0.3-1.0 seconds, but the Explainer VideoScene receives cut.transition_duration directly and does not visibly consume theme.transitionDuration in the inspected path (remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:24-39,41-105; remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:438-443). Root registers Explainer at 1920x1080, 30 fps, with metadata duration equal to the latest cut end plus one second; it also registers separate CinematicRenderer, TalkingHead, TitledVideo, CollageBurst, caption, lyric, and end-tag compositions (remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:123-151,153-331).

The OpenMontage transition contract tests are source-level assertions: they require hard-cut token handling, forwarding of transition props, local scene duration, bounded fade-out, backing color, and theme text-color propagation for chart/comparison components; they do not render frames or compare pixels (tests/contracts/test_remotion_video_transition_contract.py:7-68).

Current MPS MPVE is a Python storyboard-to-video vertical slice. VideoRequest validates topic/objective, 15-45 second duration, 16:9, analogy consent, and FHP derivation state; plan_storyboard creates a fixed storyboard rather than a Remotion cut graph (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:26-128).

MPS storyboard generation creates 3, 5, or 6 scenes by style, assigns integer scene durations by divmod, and validates positive durations, narration, visual goals, total duration, aspect ratio, and mastery check (MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:25-60,96-203,206-227).

MPS local rendering uses a single global progress value to select one scene and a scene-local progress value for deterministic Pillow drawings; it renders 1280x720 at default 24 fps and concatenates generated PNG frames with FFmpeg. There is no per-scene overlap, transition token, layout component, Remotion Sequence, or audio composition in this renderer (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:31-44,143-180,183-210).

MPS job orchestration reports queued/processing/completed/failed and coarse planning/rendering progress, writes storyboard/video/manifest artifacts, and only exposes a result after completed; its API contract explicitly treats fallback-only output as a capability issue rather than mastery evidence (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:131-177,196-241; MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:27-56).
inferences: The declared @remotion/transitions dependency appears to be reserved or legacy in this revision; the active OpenMontage transition contract is custom, local, and per-component rather than based on the package's transition primitives.
OpenMontage's composition model is a timeline/layer graph: cuts, overlays, captions, and audio can overlap independently, while each cut owns its own local duration and component animation.

The explicit sceneDurationSeconds workaround indicates a known semantic boundary: nested Sequence children cannot safely infer their own duration from useVideoConfig, so adapters must pass local duration when animation spans a cut.

OpenMontage favors deterministic frame functions. Seeded random values in CollageBurst and seeded particle logic reduce render variance, while all temporal behavior is derived from frame/fps rather than wall-clock time.

OpenMontage has two different transition abstractions: simple fade semantics for ordinary video cuts and named transform/effect presets for collage cards. They are not a single universal transition registry.

The current MPS renderer can preserve educational storyboard ordering and validation but cannot reproduce OpenMontage-like overlapping layers, local transition timing, composited overlays, or component-specific layout without a new intermediate timeline/composition representation.

OpenMontage's metadata padding of one second is an implicit final-fade safety margin; MPS currently defines total duration as the exact sum of scene durations and therefore has no equivalent tail-padding contract.
The OpenMontage tests establish source-shape contracts rather than visual behavior contracts, so passing them would not establish frame-accurate equivalence for a clean-room implementation.
unknowns: The exact runtime behavior intended by the installed @remotion/transitions package is unknown because no source import or call site was found in the inspected OpenMontage source.

The accepted values and visual semantics for ordinary transition_in/transition_out strings beyond cut and none are not enumerated in the inspected TypeScript types or contract test; non-hard values all follow the same fade path in VideoScene.
It is unknown whether transition duration should be globally theme-controlled in planned integrations; ThemeConfig exposes transitionDuration, but the inspected Explainer path does not use it.
No frame-rendered golden tests were found for scene overlap boundaries, transition clipping, progress-bar pulse/step output, collage jitter, or AnimeScene crossfades.
The exact source media duration/error behavior for OffthreadVideo when a cut's source_in_seconds exceeds media duration is not specified by the inspected contracts.

MPS has no current composition/layout schema for positions, layers, background media, captions, or audio fades, so the minimum adapter shape for importing OpenMontage-like timelines is not established.
The inspected MPS tests validate playable MP4 dimensions and API/job behavior, but do not define visual transition compatibility or a required fps beyond the local renderer defaults.
contracts: A clean-room cut timeline should accept absolute in/out times in seconds, convert them deterministically to integer frames using a declared fps, and reject or explicitly handle non-positive durations; OpenMontage demonstrates this at remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:847-855 and MPS validates positive scene durations at scripts/video_explainer.py:222-227.

Hard cut semantics must recognize cut and none case-insensitively and bypass both entrance and exit fades (OpenMontage: remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:438-456; source-level enforcement: tests/contracts/test_remotion_video_transition_contract.py:7-19).

Soft video transitions must be bounded to the local cut duration, not the full composition duration; transitionFrames must be at least one frame and fade-out must begin at max(0, localDuration-transitionFrames) (OpenMontage: remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:436-456).

Nested scene components must receive their actual local scene duration whenever their animation uses duration-dependent progress; relying on full composition duration is explicitly documented as incorrect (remotion-composer/src/components/AnimeScene.tsx:48-55,149-155).

Overlapping media layers require explicit z/layer ordering and independent active windows. OpenMontage renders cuts and overlays as sibling Sequences and keeps captions/audio outside those cut Sequences (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:846-917).

Progress values exposed to a component must be clamped to a defined range; OpenMontage clamps 0-100 and exposes deterministic fill/pulse/step modes (remotion-composer/src/components/ProgressBar.tsx:53-109).

Video source seeking must be distinct from timeline in_seconds: source_in_seconds/startFrom controls media playback offset while the Sequence/cut in-frame controls composition placement (remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:201-202,751-760; remotion-composer/src/CollageBurst.tsx:329-362).
A composition registry should declare fps, dimensions, defaults, and metadata duration policy. OpenMontage registers these explicitly per composition (remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:135-331).

MPS job/API behavior must remain separate from visual composition semantics: enqueue and poll states are queued/processing/completed/failed, and only completed jobs with an artifact are deliverable (MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:27-56; MPS-git/scripts/mpve_server.py:47-65).

Fallback/static assets must not be represented as a genuine completed video artifact; the MPS integration contract explicitly distinguishes fallback-only output from mastery evidence (MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:45-56).
mps_gaps: No MPS equivalent of OpenMontage's React/Remotion composition registry, per-composition dimensions/fps/default props, or metadata duration calculation; MPS exposes one Python MPVE service and a fixed 1280x720 local renderer (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:31-44,183-210; MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:180-241).

No MPS cut-level transition_in/transition_out/transition_duration contract, hard-cut token behavior, or local fade implementation. The current renderer switches scenes from a single global progress bucket, so it cannot overlap adjacent scene content (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:143-180).

No MPS equivalent of OpenMontage's independent layered overlays, captions, audio tracks, background image/video wrappers, or source media offset semantics (OpenMontage: remotion-composer/src/Explainer.tsx:480-553,846-917; MPS storyboard only stores scene narration/goals/assets: MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:33-60).

No MPS component dispatch/layout system for text cards, charts, KPI grids, progress bars, anime scenes, terminals, screenshots, or collage cards; storyboard visual_goal/assets are descriptive fields rather than renderable component props (MPS-git/scripts/video_explainer.py:147-190; MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:156-179).
MPS has no local-duration-aware nested scene progress equivalent to AnimeScene's effectiveDuration workaround and no multi-image crossfade contract (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:146-161).
MPS progress reporting is job lifecycle progress at 0/10/30/100, not an in-video animated progress-bar component with fill/pulse/step semantics (MPS-git/scripts/mpve_engine.py:148-150,198-228).

MPS default fps is 24 and output is 1280x720, while OpenMontage compositions conventionally use 30 fps and 1920x1080 or explicit vertical dimensions; an adapter must choose whether to resample, preserve native composition timing, or change the MPS render profile (MPS-git/scripts/hybrid_video.py:31-32; OpenMontage: remotion-composer/src/Root.tsx:138-159,271-285).

MPS test coverage proves MP4 existence/codec/dimensions and API state transitions but has no visual or frame-level tests for transitions, layout, overlap, captions, audio curves, or animated progress semantics (MPS-git/tests/test_hybrid_video.py:29-64; MPS-git/tests/test_mpve.py:49-78).
clean_room_recommendations: Define an independently authored intermediate timeline schema for MPVE with composition fps, width/height, ordered/layered clips, absolute in/out seconds, source offsets, transition descriptors, overlay windows, caption words, and audio tracks. Keep it semantic and do not reproduce OpenMontage naming or implementation text.

Implement a minimal transition engine with explicit hard-cut and fade modes first; make all transition durations local to each clip, clamp frame ranges, define behavior when a transition exceeds clip duration, and add frame-level tests for first/last visible frames and adjacent overlap.

Represent scene content as registered renderable component kinds with validated props and a fallback policy. Separate timeline placement from component-local animation duration so nested components cannot accidentally use full-composition duration.

Add layout primitives that establish absolute canvas coordinates, safe margins, z-order, background media, and aspect-ratio policy. Validate overlaps and out-of-bounds geometry before rendering rather than silently clipping educational content.

Port progress as a visual component only if required by MPS lesson design; define clamping, segmented values, label timing, and deterministic animation modes separately from API job progress to avoid conflating learner progress with render progress.

Choose and document a single MPS render profile (fps, dimensions, pixel format) and perform explicit frame/time conversion at the composition boundary. If preserving OpenMontage-like 30-fps timing, resample from the MPS 24-fps renderer or move composition into a dedicated Remotion runtime; do not silently mix rates.

Add deterministic golden-frame or perceptual snapshot tests for hard cuts, fades, overlapping scenes, local nested durations, background overlays, progress modes, and vertical/landscape layouts. Retain API tests for job lifecycle independently.

Treat AGPL-3.0 OpenMontage as reference-only for clean-room work: use observed contracts and behavior descriptions, write new schemas and implementation, avoid copying source/assets/text, and maintain provenance notes separating facts, inferences, and independently designed decisions.

Preserve the existing MPS pedagogical boundary: composition should consume an already validated storyboard/request and must not decide mastery, reveal an unearned derivation, or treat a fallback artifact as evidence of learning (MPS-git/docs/mpve-integration.md:5-42; MPS-git/docs/mpve-api.md:45-56).
